findings.title: All-groups VIEW permission is treated as manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, so a caller who only has the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. requireManage() is the gate for creating top-level groups (GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup). That caller can therefore create groups despite having only view access. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, so the no-arg check is inconsistent with per-group enforcement and with the security model. The interface javadoc repeats the same VIEW-or-MANAGE rule and should be corrected with the implementation.

findings.title: Group view filter stores authz resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission treats its argument as a group id and looks the resource up with findByName. Instance group resources are named with the group id (resolveGroup returns group.getId()), while Resource.getId() is the authorization resource primary key, so the lookup misses the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource. The id added to the set is also not a group id. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource put that set on the session as UserModel.GROUPS and pass it to getUsersCount. A non-empty set of authz ids makes user search and counts match no real groups (admins with view-members see nobody). The all-groups type resource itself is included by findByType; if it has view-members, its internal id is added and poisons the same filter. The set should contain resource names that are actual group ids, and the type resource named "Groups" must be skipped. Current tests still pass when the set stays empty because listing post-filters with canView, so they do not catch a wrong or empty id set on the count/search path.

findings.title: Per-group authz resources are created without a type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the instance resource with resourceStore.create and updates scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). The schema init path does set type on the type-level resources, which shows create() does not infer it. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission depends on resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Group resources created for fine-grained permissions therefore are not returned, so view-members and manage-members grants on specific groups are invisible to user search and user-count filtering.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never gain Groups scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else reconciles the schema. Realms that enabled fine-grained admin permissions before this change keep a resource server that has no Groups type resource and no manage-membership, manage-members, or view-members scopes. Creating a group permission then hits getOrCreateResource, which throws ModelException("No scopes found.") when a schema scope is missing. Evaluations that fall back to getResourceTypeResource("Groups") get null, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission calls policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes() on that null, turning a missing schema into a 500 instead of a deny.

findings.title: V2 group permission management throws and breaks group deletion
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, and the policy accessors) always throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and the GroupRemovedEvent listener still calls groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is also enabled. Deleting a group then fails the listener with UnsupportedOperationException and can roll back the delete. The same throw hits the group management/permissions admin endpoints, which still require the V1 feature and then call these methods. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all, so deleting a group leaves its authorization resources and policies behind with no V2 cleanup.

findings.title: Permission resource names are not resolved for groups
findings.body: getResourceName special-cases only the Users type and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group instance resources are created with the group id as the name and no display name, and this change never adds a Groups branch that loads the group and returns its name or path. Permission listings for the new Groups resource type therefore show null (or a raw id) instead of a group name, and a missing group is not reported the way a missing user is.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers is false. Callers reading only the contract will enforce or test membership management instead of member management.
